surfaceForm: University of Luxembourg (recurring throughout, e.g. "members of the academic community of the University of Luxembourg")
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:stakeholders (On the nature of this report) and ~40 other occurrences
proposedGenericDecision: Replace with role-based generic "the institution" / "the University" / "a research-and-teaching university" — the home institution adopting the policy.
rationale: The document is hard-wired to one named university. The single most pervasive non-agnostic anchor; appears in stakeholder boxes, reading guide, regulatory analysis, governance, costs and conclusion.

surfaceForm: Board of Governors / \institution{Board of Governors} / Conseil de Gouvernance
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:stakeholders; sec:reading-guide; sec:exec-training; tab:transition
proposedGenericDecision: Use a role-based label for the supreme governing body (e.g. "the governing board" / "the top governance body").
rationale: "Board of Governors"/"Conseil de Gouvernance" is UL's specific top-body name. The macro \institution{Board of Governors} bakes a UL-specific governance shape into the prose.

surfaceForm: Faculty Council, University Council (the "University Bodies")
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:stakeholders; sec:reading-guide; sec:dpc; decision-flow
proposedGenericDecision: Role-based: "faculty-level council" and "institution-level academic council"; generalize "University Bodies" to "the institution's deliberative bodies".
rationale: Specific tri-layer body structure (Faculty Council -> University Council -> Board of Governors) is UL's statutory decision path; the endorsement chain is repeated as an institutional fact.

surfaceForm: Rectorate / the Rector
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:stakeholders; sec:exec-training ("the Rector and the members of the Conseil de Gouvernance")
proposedGenericDecision: Use role-based "the executive leadership" / "the head of the institution and the executive board".
rationale: "Rectorate"/"Rector" presumes a rector-led continental-European governance shape; not institution-agnostic (US institutions use President/Provost; UK use Vice-Chancellor).

surfaceForm: Tri-faculty assumption: "the University of Luxembourg — which comprises three faculties, each with departments of teaching and research, and interdisciplinary centres"
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:dpc
proposedGenericDecision: Generalize to "the institution's faculties/schools and interdisciplinary centres" without hard-coding a count.
rationale: Hard-codes UL's specific three-faculty + interdisciplinary-centre structure as the worked example for the Digital Policy Commission composition.

surfaceForm: UL-specific entity taxonomy: "research-only units, research-and-teaching departments, and teaching/training-only components"
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:introduction; tab:besoins note (l.1631); sec:specificites; icradp mission
proposedGenericDecision: Generalize to mission-based categories (research, teaching, mixed) without UL's exact organizational-unit nomenclature; or keep as an instantiation example clearly labelled as such.
rationale: The triple taxonomy (and the note that 'research-and-teaching departments span two zones') reflects UL's specific organizational chart; the underlying mission distinction is generic but the named unit types are local.

surfaceForm: Luxembourg transposition of NIS2 = project of law 8364 (PL 8364) with cited articles 2(34°), 11(1)(4°), 2(40°), 12(1), 12(2), 12(3), 11(4), 21
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:reading-guide; sec:nis2; sec:lu-landscape; sec:obligations-mapping; sec:advocacy; principlebox; sec:propositions; tab:transition (~25+ refs)
proposedGenericDecision: Parameterize the national-transposition instrument: replace "project of law 8364" and its article numbering with a placeholder "the national NIS2 transposition law" plus a localization table of article references; keep the generic NIS2 Directive articles.
rationale: PL 8364 and its precise article-number pegs are Luxembourg-specific. A national-transposition assumption is stated as binding; another country has a different instrument and numbering. Core load-bearing legal anchor of the whole defensibility argument.

surfaceForm: Project of law 8307 transposing the CER Directive (EU) 2022/2557
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:reglementation methodology note; sec:lu-landscape (Concomitant CER framework)
proposedGenericDecision: Parameterize: "the national CER-directive transposition"; keep generic CER Directive (EU) 2022/2557.
rationale: PL 8307 is the Luxembourg CER transposition instrument; jurisdiction-specific.

surfaceForm: ILR — Institut Luxembourgeois de Régulation (\gls{ilr}), the national supervisory authority
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:stakeholders; sec:nis2; sec:lu-landscape; sec:advocacy; sec:exec-training; sec:propositions; tab:transition (~25+ refs)
proposedGenericDecision: Role-based: "the national NIS2 supervisory authority".
rationale: ILR is Luxembourg's designated NIS2 supervisor; every "report submitted to the ILR" / "confirmed by the ILR" is jurisdiction-bound.

surfaceForm: GOVCERT.LU (\gls{govcertlu}) — governmental CSIRT
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:stakeholders (Luxembourg context); sec:lu-landscape; sec:propositions (Shared Security Organizations)
proposedGenericDecision: Role-based: "the national/governmental CSIRT".
rationale: GOVCERT.LU is the Luxembourg governmental CSIRT designated as the University's first-line CSIRT; jurisdiction-specific operational chain.

surfaceForm: HCPN — Haut-Commissariat à la Protection nationale (\gls{hcpn})
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:stakeholders; sec:lu-landscape; sec:advocacy; sec:propositions
proposedGenericDecision: Role-based: "the national single-point-of-contact for NIS2 cooperation".
rationale: HCPN is Luxembourg's NIS2 single point of contact and host of GOVCERT.LU/ANSSI-LU; jurisdiction-specific.

surfaceForm: ANSSI Luxembourg / ANSSI-LU (\gls{anssilu}), national Agency for Information Systems Security
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:stakeholders; sec:lu-landscape (Public-sector reference framework); sec:advocacy
proposedGenericDecision: Role-based: "the national information-systems-security agency".
rationale: ANSSI-LU is the Luxembourg state infosec agency (note the document itself disambiguates it from the French ANSSI). Jurisdiction-specific.

surfaceForm: PSI-LU — Politique générale de la sécurité de l'information de l'État luxembourgeois (\gls{psilu})
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:stakeholders; sec:reglementation methodology note; sec:lu-landscape (Public-sector reference framework)
proposedGenericDecision: Role-based: "the national public-sector information-security baseline policy".
rationale: PSI-LU is the Luxembourg State infosec policy; the architecture is positioned as 'a compatible operational implementation that adapts the PSI-LU baseline'. Jurisdiction-bound.

surfaceForm: SERIMA (SEcurity RIsk MAnagement) national incident-notification platform, operational since 2 May 2025
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:stakeholders; sec:lu-landscape; tab:reglementation; tab:obligations-essentielles; sec:normes (MONARC); tab:transition; sec:propositions
proposedGenericDecision: Role-based: "the national incident-notification platform"; keep the generic NIS2 24h/72h/30-day cadence (which is Directive-level, not national).
rationale: SERIMA is the Luxembourg single national platform operated by ILR; another jurisdiction reports through a different system. The 24/72/30 cadence is generic and should be kept.

surfaceForm: NCSS III — third National Cybersecurity Strategy (2018), Implementation Objective 7
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:stakeholders; sec:lu-landscape (National strategy hook); sec:advocacy (C.4); sec:safeguards-ai positioning
proposedGenericDecision: Role-based: "the national cybersecurity strategy's academic-cooperation objective".
rationale: NCSS III Objective 7 (approved by the Luxembourg Government Council on 26 Jan 2018, published by HCPN) is the national political hook; jurisdiction-specific.

surfaceForm: MONARC risk-analysis methodology (developed by NC3 under the Luxembourg House of Cybersecurity); "NC3"; "Luxembourg House of Cybersecurity"
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:reading-guide; sec:normes (MONARC subsection); sec:safeguards positioning; sec:propositions; tab:transition
proposedGenericDecision: Generalize: present MONARC as one option alongside ISO/IEC 27005; describe it as "a national open-source risk-analysis method" and let the generic ISO 27005 carry the agnostic version.
rationale: MONARC is Luxembourg-developed and politically resonant locally ('carries a specific operational and political relevance'); ISO/IEC 27005 is the generic fallback the document already offers in parallel.

surfaceForm: CNPD (\institution{CNPD}) — Luxembourg national data protection authority
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:lu-landscape (SERIMA partners); sec:safeguards-ai advocacy positioning; sec:advocacy D.5
proposedGenericDecision: Role-based: "the national data protection authority".
rationale: CNPD is Luxembourg's DPA; cited as a SERIMA partner and a recipient of the report's register template. Jurisdiction-specific.

surfaceForm: CIRCL (\gls{circl}) — Luxembourg CSIRT for private sector / communes / NGOs
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:lu-landscape (ecosystem disambiguation); sec:propositions (Shared Security Organizations)
proposedGenericDecision: Drop or generalize: the disambiguation paragraph is Luxembourg-ecosystem-specific; in a generic version, reference "sector/private CSIRTs as relevant for third-party partners".
rationale: CIRCL is named only for Luxembourg-ecosystem disambiguation against GOVCERT.LU; not load-bearing for the argument and Luxembourg-bound.

surfaceForm: CSSF (\gls{cssf}) — Luxembourg financial-sector supervisor
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:lu-landscape (ecosystem disambiguation, 'not competent for the University outside specific financial projects')
proposedGenericDecision: Drop: financial-sector-supervisor disambiguation is Luxembourg-specific and non-essential.
rationale: CSSF is mentioned only to clarify it is NOT competent; Luxembourg-ecosystem disambiguation with no generic value.

surfaceForm: RESTENA — Luxembourg NREN (\gls{restena}, \institution{...}) and RESTENA-CSIRT
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:reading-guide; sec:exemples panel; subsec:lux-sdmz-status; sec:nren; sec:propositions; sec:couts; fig:archi-proposee (Internet/RESTENA/GÉANT)
proposedGenericDecision: Role-based: "the national research-and-education network (NREN)" with GÉANT kept as the generic European backbone; parameterize the NREN-CSIRT.
rationale: RESTENA is Luxembourg's specific NREN; the document repeatedly anchors connectivity, the Science DMZ feasibility and federated identity to it. GÉANT and the NREN concept are generic and should be kept.

surfaceForm: ULHPC, MeluXina (EuroHPC), LIST, LIH — Luxembourg research ecosystem
location: main-body-EN.tex :: subsec:lux-sdmz-status (Luxembourg status / federated Science DMZ reframing)
proposedGenericDecision: Generalize the entire 'Luxembourg status' subsection to a role-based 'national research ecosystem' framing, or mark it as a localization annex; replace named peers (LIST, LIH) and facilities (ULHPC, MeluXina) with role labels.
rationale: The 'mutualised, NREN-anchored Science DMZ' argument is built entirely on Luxembourg's small-ecosystem reality (University + LIST + LIH, ULHPC/MeluXina). Both the named peers and the smallness premise are jurisdiction-specific.

surfaceForm: Smallness premise: "Luxembourg's research ecosystem (...) is too small for three separate Science DMZs"; "~12,000 students, comparable to the University of Luxembourg"
location: main-body-EN.tex :: subsec:lux-sdmz-status; sec:exemples (EPFL size comparison, Track record paragraph)
proposedGenericDecision: Generalize: frame mutualisation as scale-dependent ('where the national ecosystem is small, an NREN-anchored shared zone is rational') without hard-coding Luxembourg's size or a 12,000-student peer comparison.
rationale: The size-comparability and 'too small for three DMZs' reasoning encodes Luxembourg's specific small-country scale; a larger jurisdiction would not share the premise.

surfaceForm: "In a country that is among the wealthiest in the world, and whose governance bodies set excellence as the sole objective"; "the university's multi-year agreement with the State"
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:couts (intro and feasibility); sec:stakeholders (feasibility 'university multi-year plan')
proposedGenericDecision: Generalize the wealth/excellence framing to neutral 'within the institution's multi-year planning and funding agreement'; drop the 'wealthiest country' rhetorical anchor.
rationale: The 'wealthiest country' and 'multi-year agreement with the State' framing presumes Luxembourg's specific funding model (convention pluriannuelle); not institution-agnostic.

surfaceForm: ILR essential-entity classification letter "notified to the Department of Computer Science on 3 April 2026" (\cite{ilr-ul-essential})
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:reading-guide (Luxembourg-specific context, Status); sec:nis2
proposedGenericDecision: Generalize: 'the institution has been (or expects to be) classified as an essential entity by the national supervisory authority'; drop the specific notification date and recipient department.
rationale: A specific dated classification event addressed to UL's Department of Computer Science; concrete institution-and-date fact that cannot survive generalization as stated.

surfaceForm: Department of Computer Science (DCS) — pilot entity and 'hosts a Department of Computer Science whose research portfolio covers information-systems security'
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:nis2; sec:advocacy (Position D, D.3); sec:couts; tab:transition (Pilot); l.3940
proposedGenericDecision: Generalize to role-based 'the institution's computer-science / information-security research unit' as a natural pilot candidate.
rationale: DCS is UL's specific unit, used both as the moral-authority basis ('hosting a Department of Computer Science') and as the named pilot site. The role (a CS/security unit) is generalizable; the specific name is not.

surfaceForm: SnT — Interdisciplinary Centre for Security, Reliability and Trust
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:couts (pilot); tab:transition (Pilot step); l.3940
proposedGenericDecision: Generalize to 'a security/reliability interdisciplinary research centre' as a co-pilot candidate.
rationale: SnT is UL's specific interdisciplinary centre named as a pilot site; institution-specific.

surfaceForm: "the university's HPC team" (named pilot entity alongside DCS and SnT)
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:couts; tab:transition; l.3940
proposedGenericDecision: Generalize to 'the institution's HPC operations team' — already nearly role-based, just needs INSTITUTION_NAME removed.
rationale: Tied to the UL pilot trio; the 'university's HPC team' is generic in role but bound to the named institution's pilot scoping.

surfaceForm: Committee for Reasonable Adjustments — "The University of Luxembourg already has a Committee for Reasonable Adjustments" (\cite{unilu-amenagements})
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:commission-ajustements (The precedent of the University of Luxembourg)
proposedGenericDecision: Generalize to 'many institutions already operate a reasonable-adjustments committee for students/staff'; reframe the UL-precedent subsection as a generic 'existing-mechanism' argument or mark it as a localization example.
rationale: An entire subsection is built on UL's specific existing committee as the analogical precedent for ICRADP; the coherence argument ('if the university already operates X...') is institution-specific.

surfaceForm: Université Paris-Saclay ransomware (Aug 2024, RansomHouse, ~1 TB, worked with ANSSI); Université de Rennes (Mar 2025, FunkSec, ISTIC subnet); Sorbonne Université (2024)
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:defaillances-mediatiques (France subsubsection); sec:stakeholders; sec:exemples (French universities)
proposedGenericDecision: Keep as evidence (these are public incidents serving a generic argument), but the French national-agency reference (ANSSI = French ANSSI) and the implicit 'French equivalent of the Luxembourg framework' comparison should be neutralized to 'the relevant national cybersecurity agency'.
rationale: Named incidents are public-domain evidence supporting a country-agnostic thesis (segmentation limits blast radius), so they can stay; but the French-ANSSI mention and the 'French equivalent of the Luxembourg framework' framing in sec:exemples are jurisdiction-comparative and should be generalized. Flagged per the brief's 'named incidents' criterion.

surfaceForm: "Paris-Saclay (multi-institution federation in a public-research perimeter regulated under the French equivalent of the Luxembourg framework)"
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:exemples (Relevant and Adequate Reference panel, criterion 3)
proposedGenericDecision: Generalize 'the French equivalent of the Luxembourg framework' to 'a comparable national public-research regulatory framework'.
rationale: Explicitly frames the comparison relative to 'the Luxembourg framework', a non-agnostic anchor embedded in the institutional-benchmark panel.

surfaceForm: ICRADP (Independent Commission for Reasonable Adjustments of Digital Policies; fr: CARPN)
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:stakeholders; sec:commission-ajustements (title and proposal); multiple cross-refs
proposedGenericDecision: Keep the role/concept (an independent reasonable-adjustments commission) as a generic proposal; drop the bilingual French 'CARPN' gloss which presumes a French-language institutional context.
rationale: ICRADP itself is a proposed generic body, but the 'fr: CARPN' French acronym and the assumption of a French/multilingual administrative setting are local. The concept is portable; the bilingual labelling is not.

surfaceForm: Luxembourg Law of 28 November 2006 transposing Directive 2000/78/EC (\cite{lux-loi-2006})
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:commission-ajustements (European Equal Treatment and Disability Law)
proposedGenericDecision: Parameterize: 'the national transposition of Directive 2000/78/EC integrates the reasonable-adjustment obligation into national labour law'; keep the generic Directive and CRPD.
rationale: The 28 Nov 2006 law is Luxembourg's specific transposition; the EU Directive 2000/78/EC and CRPD above it are generic and should remain.

surfaceForm: CRPD "ratified by the EU and by Luxembourg"
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:commission-ajustements (CRPD bullet)
proposedGenericDecision: Generalize to 'ratified by the EU and its member states' / 'by the relevant jurisdiction'.
rationale: The '...and by Luxembourg' clause hard-codes the home jurisdiction into an otherwise generic CRPD reference.

surfaceForm: Essential-entity classification 'on the basis of its status as a public institution' — public-institution premise specific to UL's legal status
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:stakeholders; sec:nis2; sec:reading-guide
proposedGenericDecision: Generalize the classification rationale to 'on the basis of the institution's status under the national transposition'; recognise that a private or differently-statused university would have a different peg.
rationale: The whole 'public-administration entity, essential regardless of size' chain assumes UL's public-institution legal status under PL 8364; institutions with other statuses (or in other jurisdictions) reach essential/important classification by different routes.

surfaceForm: French IT-charter precedents: UPPA (\cite{uppa-charte}), Le Havre (\cite{lehavre-charte}), 'in France, CNRS and universities'
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:exemples (Organizational models: charters and accountability)
proposedGenericDecision: Keep as institutional-precedent evidence (Layer 5), but ensure they are framed as illustrative international examples, not as the home-jurisdiction norm; no change needed beyond context.
rationale: These are external precedents (France) used as evidence, consistent with the institutional-benchmark panel; they are not the home institution and do not break agnosticism. Logged for completeness.

surfaceForm: Reference-university panel: MIT, Stanford, Cambridge, ETH Zurich, CMU, Michigan, CERN, Oxford, EPFL, Wisconsin-Madison, NC State, Penn State, Paris-Saclay, Sorbonne, CNRS model
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:exemples (entire section); tab:comparatif; sec:propositions (P15)
proposedGenericDecision: Keep — these are external institutional precedents (evidence Layer 5) and are inherently part of a benchmark, not the home institution.
rationale: The state-of-the-art panel of named peer universities is legitimate comparative evidence and should remain; it does not bind the document to UL. Logged so the matrix records the deliberate keep-decision.

surfaceForm: \institution{...} semantic macro used with UL-specific bodies (Board of Governors, ILR, CNPD, Luxembourg House of Cybersecurity)
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:stakeholders; sec:nis2; sec:lu-landscape; sec:safeguards-ai
proposedGenericDecision: Where \institution{} wraps a localized body name, the inner string should resolve from a localization variable rather than a hard-coded UL/Luxembourg term.
rationale: The brief explicitly flags 'a macro that expands to a UL term'. The \institution{} macro itself is generic, but several of its arguments are hard-coded Luxembourg-specific names that should be driven by localization variables.

surfaceForm: Localized glossary entries: \gls{ilr}, \gls{govcertlu}, \gls{hcpn}, \gls{anssilu}, \gls{psilu}, \gls{serima}, \gls{restena}, \gls{circl}, \gls{cssf}, \gls{monarc}, \gls{icradp}, \gls{nis2} national pegs
location: main-body-EN.tex :: used throughout; definitions live in a separate glossary file (not this body file)
proposedGenericDecision: Audit the glossary so each Luxembourg-specific \gls{} acronym maps to a localization-driven definition or is replaced by a role-based gls key (e.g. \gls{nren} instead of \gls{restena}).
rationale: Many \gls{} keys expand to Luxembourg-named entities. The brief flags 'a macro that expands to a UL term'; \gls expansions are the systematic vector for this. Definitions are out-of-file but every usage in this body propagates the localization.

surfaceForm: MeluXina (EuroHPC) as the petabyte-scale research-traffic destination
location: main-body-EN.tex :: subsec:lux-sdmz-status
proposedGenericDecision: Generalize to 'a national/EuroHPC supercomputing facility'; keep EuroHPC as the generic European programme.
rationale: MeluXina is Luxembourg's specific EuroHPC system; the Science DMZ feasibility traffic-profile argument anchors to it.

surfaceForm: Recurrent 'campus' / 'campus perimeter' / 'campus network core' framing in the Science DMZ and architecture sections
location: main-body-EN.tex :: subsec:science-dmz; fig:science-dmz; fig:archi-proposee; subsec:vlan; tab:vlans (Residential/student residences)
proposedGenericDecision: Generalize 'campus' to 'site(s)' where the architecture must support multi-site / multi-data-centre institutions; the Science DMZ 'campus enclave' is already softened by the NREN-circuit alternative.
rationale: The 'campus' vocabulary mildly assumes a single-campus topology. The document already offers the NREN-operated alternative to a 'campus enclave', so the assumption is partly mitigated; flagged as the brief asks for the implicit single-campus assumption.

surfaceForm: "Prior practice in the Luxembourg public sector did not formalise such a multi-zone approach"; positioning as model 'for peer public-administration entities'
location: main-body-EN.tex :: sec:advocacy (B.3); sec:lu-landscape (PSI-LU adaptation)
proposedGenericDecision: Generalize to 'prior national public-sector practice'; replace 'peer public-administration entities' with a role-based phrase.
rationale: These claims position the architecture relative to the Luxembourg public-sector status quo; jurisdiction-bound contribution framing.
